title: M 408C or M 408N (Differential and Integral Calculus)
description: A first calculus course: limits, derivatives and their applications, and an introduction to integrals. Some universities offer it as one accelerated course and others split the same material over a longer sequence.
notes: Choice slot: UT's accelerated M 408C or the first course of the M 408N/408S/408M sequence. Official descriptions are in data/raw/utaustin/ (courses-m page).

title: M 408D or M 408S (Sequences, Series, and Multivariable Calculus)
description: A second calculus course: techniques and applications of integration and, in accelerated versions, sequences, series, and an introduction to multivariable calculus.
notes: Choice slot: UT's M 408D (accelerated sequence) or M 408S (second course of the three-course sequence, followed by M 408M). Official descriptions are in data/raw/utaustin/ (courses-m page).

title: SDS 321 or M 362K (Introduction to Probability and Statistics)
description: A calculus-based introduction to probability: random variables, common distributions, expectation, and limit theorems, sometimes with an introduction to statistical inference.
notes: Choice slot: UT's SDS 321 or M 362K. Official descriptions are in data/raw/utaustin/ (courses-sds and courses-m pages).

title: U.S. History (060)
description: A general education course in United States history, often a survey of the nation's political, social, and economic development. Many public universities in the U.S. require such courses by state law.
notes: Texas Core Curriculum component 060 (American History); UT's plan has two courses (6 hours).

title: Social and Behavioral Sciences (080)
description: A general education course on how individuals, groups, and societies behave, from a field such as psychology, sociology, economics, or anthropology. These courses introduce the field's research methods and main theories.

title: First-Year Signature Course (090)
description: A small first-year seminar on a topic chosen by the instructor, emphasizing discussion, writing, and university-level inquiry. These courses also introduce students to the university's resources.
notes: Texas Core Curriculum component 090 at UT; approved by the departmental advisor.

title: Visual and Performing Arts (050)
description: A general education course in the arts, such as art history, music, theatre, dance, or film. These courses build an understanding of artistic works and how they are made.

title: Humanities (040)
description: A general education course in the humanities, such as literature, philosophy, or cultural studies, focused on reading and interpreting texts and ideas.
notes: Texas Core Curriculum component 040 (Language, Philosophy and Culture).

title: Natural Science and Technology, Part I (030)
description: A natural science course, often part of a two-course sequence in biology, chemistry, or physics, that introduces the field's main ideas and methods, sometimes with a laboratory.
notes: Texas Core Curriculum component 030, filled at UT by the major's two-course science sequence (see notes on the rows).

title: Foreign Language and Culture
description: A course in a language other than English, or in the culture of a language area. Programs with this requirement usually ask for beginning proficiency or a pair of related courses.
notes: UT degree requirement: 6 hours (language plus culture, or two culture courses).

title: Upper-division C S elective
description: An upper-level computer science course chosen by the student from the department's offerings, such as operating systems, networks, databases, artificial intelligence, security, or graphics.
notes: UT: 24 hours of upper-division C S beyond the core (major plus Computer Science Option).

title: Math or Science course
description: An additional mathematics or natural science course chosen from an approved list, such as a further course in a science sequence or an upper-division mathematics course.
notes: UT: one course from the listed options (3 hours).

title: Free Elective
description: Any course the student chooses that counts toward the degree, inside or outside the major.
notes: UT: hours needed to reach the 120-hour total (19 in the plan).
